text:
Maya: Hey folks — noticed a recurring mismatch between billed GPU credits and what our SLO dashboards show per-tenant. Billing says tenant A used ~2.1k GPU-hours last week, but our Grafana tenant rollup shows ~1.6k. Any ideas where attribution is leaking?

Chris: Is this the Prometheus-derived metric or the billing export?

Maya: Grafana is pulling from Prometheus recording rules (we use `tenant_gpu_seconds_total` derived from `gpu_allocated_seconds_total{tenant_id=~".*"}`), billing is the warehouse export. The gap is pretty consistent (~20-25%).

Bina: Could be label cardinality or missing label on some export paths. If some kube controllers allocate without tenant label we would undercount in Prom.

Sam: Agree. Quick check: any pods in GPU pools missing the `tenant_id` label?

Leo: Ran a quick grep on live metadata: `kubectl get pods -n gpu-pool -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.metadata.labels.tenant_id}{"\n"}{end}'` — found ~120 pods with blank label last week (they were preemption/burst jobs).

Maya: Ugh. Those are likely burst pods started by the cheaper fallback scaler (no tenant id because they use pooled service-account). That could explain undercount. But billing still charges them to tenant via reservation mapping, so Prom is missing them.

Chris: Two immediate fixes: 1) backfill metrics by joining kube pod labels + allocation events into a new exporter or recording rule; 2) enforce label injection at admission time so future pods always have tenant_id.

Bina: For backfill — we can create a Prom recording rule that sums `gpu_seconds` by joining `pod:gpu_allocated:sum` with a `kube_pod_labels` metric that has `tenant_id`. But Prom doesn't do joins across metrics well. Better to write a short exporter that emits `gpu_allocated_seconds_total{tenant_id=...}` by watching the API.

Sam: I can hack an exporter (go) to watch pods and allocations and emit the combined metric. Will that fix historical gaps? We only have billing history in warehouse.

Leo: For historical reconciliation we need to compute the delta from kube events & node allocation logs and then push a synthetic metric series to a long-term metrics store or a CSV for billing team. Might be easier to compute a tenant attribution table offline and store in the warehouse; then update Grafana to pull from warehouse for cost dashboards instead of Prom for that timeframe.

Maya: Priority: (A) short-term reconciliation for last 30 days; (B) prevent recurrence. Suggestions on recording rules / alerts we should add until admission controller is in place?

Chris: Add an alert that fires when `sum(rate(gpu_allocated_seconds_total[1d])) by (tenant_id)` differs from `billing_tenant_gpu_seconds` by > 10% for >48h. Use `abs((prom - bill)/bill) > 0.1`. Example query:

```
abs((sum_over_time(prom:tenant_gpu_seconds[7d]) - warehouse:tenant_gpu_seconds[7d]) / warehouse:tenant_gpu_seconds[7d])) > 0.10
```

(We'll need a `warehouse:tenant_gpu_seconds` metric pulled into Prom via the remote_write or exported as a federation metric.)

Bina: If we don't want warehouse metrics in Prom, Grafana can do the comparison in a dashboard panel (transformations) and we can use an alerting channel there (Grafana alerting supports mixed data sources now). But SRE alerting lives in PromAlert; mixing may be awkward.

Maya: OpsBot: can you list recent alerts for `gpu-attr-mismatch` so we know if this already fired?

OpsBot: Alert query history: no `gpu-attr-mismatch` alerts recorded in the last 90d. Noted incidents referencing "unattributed GPU usage" at 1760200000 and 1762100000.

Sam: For the admission controller: small webhook that copies `tenant_id` from pod template annotations or service-account mapping. I can prototype. Anyone have objections to requiring `tenant_id` on all GPU pod nausea?

Leo: We need an exception flow for system/burst jobs that legitimately should not be billed to a tenant (eg autoscaler scratch tasks). Maybe a `tenant_id=__shared_pool__` label. But then we must ensure billing maps that to pool owner.

Chris: Also consider recording per-node GPU assignment spans in a vectorized metric: `node_gpu_binding_seconds{node, tenant_id}` so we capture allocations even if pod labels absent. Node agents already log binding events, so exporter can sum them. That avoids relying solely on pod labels.

Bina: On dashboard side, suggest adding an 'Attribution Confidence' panel: % of GPU seconds with explicit tenant_id vs total. Quick Prom query: `sum(gpu_allocated_seconds_total{tenant_id!=""}) / sum(gpu_allocated_seconds_total)` over 7d. Alert if < 0.9 for >72h.

Maya: Good. Who wants to own short-term exporter + dashboard tweak? Also we need a small RFC for the admission controller and exception policy.

Sam: I'll own the exporter and backfill script (I'll open a draft PR by EOD).

Leo: I'll add the dashboard panel and a Grafana-level alert.

Chris: I'll draft the RFC for admission controller + exception mapping and the PromAlert rule for the mismatch.

Bina: I'll coordinate with Billing team to export `billing_tenant_gpu_seconds` as either a Prom federation endpoint or a daily CSV we can ingest.

Maya: Thanks all. Sam — ping @oncall if exporter touches production metrics ingestion. Also tag me on the PR.

Sam: Will do. Starting with a local watcher that emits to `custom/tenant_gpu_seconds_total` via pushgateway for backfill, then move to scrape endpoint.

Leo: Quick note: when backfilling, keep metric names and labels consistent to avoid creating new series explosion. Use `tenant_id` label only and keep cardinality limited.

Maya: Cool — let's reconvene in 48h with PRs/patches. :thumbsup:
